html:
Port is a sweet fortified wine from the Douro valley in northern Portugal, shipped from Porto. In 1756 the Douro became one of the first wine regions in the world with legal boundaries.

English merchants built the trade in the late 1600s, when wars with France cut off French wine. The Methuen Treaty of 1703 gave Portuguese wine low duties in England. Adding brandy to stop fermentation kept the wine sweet and strong for the voyage. British firms with names like Taylor and Croft still make it.

The Marquis of Pombal created a state company and the demarcated region to control quality and break British dominance. The terraced vineyards of the Douro are a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The trade is a product of the Anglo-Portuguese Alliance. See Portugal.
sum: Port is a sweet fortified wine from the Douro valley in northern Portugal, shipped from Porto. In 1756 the Douro became one of the first wine regions in the world with legal boundaries.
